channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Governo dá como certo tarifaço de 25%, mas vê chance de ampliar lista de exceções
item.description: The Brazilian government considers it certain that the U.S. will impose a 25% tariff on Brazilian goods, but hopes to expand the list of exceptions through technical negotiations. The final decision is expected by July 15, with a possible marginal discount, though observers believe it is more likely that the USTR will add new sectors to the exception list based on technical assessments of supply chain impacts. Flávio Bolsonaro was the only one among 34 Brazilians at the U.S. public hearing who did not oppose the measures, instead suggesting a delay with clear electoral motives.

item.title: O poder de Michelle é oficial. Péssima notícia para Flávio.
item.description: The Meio/Ideia poll shows Michelle Bolsonaro as Brazil’s most powerful woman with 15.4% of mentions, far ahead of Janja at 9%. This confirms her role as a conservative leader and potential electoral asset for the right, which poses a serious problem for Flávio Bolsonaro, who is currently in open conflict with her. The family rift, fueled by allegations of humiliation from Bolsonaro’s sons, has isolated Flávio from the main political force within his own clan, weakening his candidacy due to arrogance and poor strategy.

item.title: Vista como 'traidora' por grupo de Michelle, Bia Kicis defende candidatura da ex-primeira-dama: 'Vaga é dela'
item.description: Bia Kicis, Senate pre-candidate from DF, publicly defended Michelle Bolsonaro's Senate candidacy, stating the seat 'belongs to her', following tensions with Michelle's group over a video criticizing Flávio Bolsonaro. Kicis said she supports the duo on the PL ticket despite recent disagreements.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro segue em queda com alternativas em análise nas pesquisas
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro has been in constant decline in polls for three months, having been overtaken by Lula, who leads but with high rejection near 50%. The senator's decline has sparked speculation about alternative far-right candidacies, particularly Michelle Bolsonaro, who in hypothetical second-round scenarios would have majority support among men (42.1%), while women back Lula by a wide margin (50.3%). The election is becoming increasingly unpredictable due to high rejection of both main candidates and the lack of defined political identity among over 20,000 legislative candidates.

item.title: STF valida cota racial em fundos partidário e eleitoral
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court validated the constitutional amendment allocating 30% of Party Fund and FEFC resources to Black and brown candidacies, allowing future compensation without immediate sanctions for past non-compliance. The 6-4 ruling rejected claims of unconstitutionality and violation of electoral annuality, affirming Congress’s authority to set minimum percentages within constitutional limits.

item.title: A disputa e o acordo por trás da reconciliação entre Benedita e Quaquá
item.description: Washington Quaquá, mayor of Maricá and national vice-president of the PT, reversed his ageist criticisms of Benedita da Silva’s Senate candidacy after pressure from allies, including Eduardo Paes and Pedro Paulo of the PSD, to ensure a smooth campaign slate. The reconciliation followed a meeting at Quaquá’s residence and was followed by his official appointment as coordinator of Lula’s campaign in Rio de Janeiro, with João Maurício as subcoordinator. Despite the agreement, there are internal PT concerns about potential future outbursts by Quaquá during the campaign.

item.title: Tebet rebate Tarcísio, que a criticou por concorrer em SP: 'Não precisei dar endereço alheio'
item.description: Simone Tebet rebutted Tarcísio de Freitas' criticism of her Senate candidacy in São Paulo, stating she has paid taxes in the state for 10 years and did not need to use a 'foreign address' to run. She emphasized her identity as a Corinthians fan and her established political trajectory in SP, contrasting with claims that she and Marina Silva received a 'red card' from their home states. Tebet indirectly referenced the archived investigation into Tarcísio's 2022 domicile change to São José dos Campos.

item.title: O governo Lula está com medo
item.description: The Lula government has decided to tighten communication rules for ministers and second- and third-tier officials to avoid accusations of electoral campaigning by Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign. Based on a recommendation from Attorney General Jorge Messias, ministries must now use more institutional language when announcing government actions, aiming to preserve administrative neutrality.

item.title: Flávio sinaliza definição sobre candidato ao Senado no Rio
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro signaled to interlocutors that he intends to define the Senate candidate for Rio de Janeiro by the end of the week, indicating a possible advancement in the Bolsonarist candidacy articulation in the state. The information was disclosed in a subscriber-exclusive article requiring registration for full access. The move suggests the naming of the candidate may be imminent, following weeks of speculation.

item.title: Ministros divergem de orientação do Planalto para redes na eleição
item.description: Lula government ministers are dissatisfied with Planalto and AGU rules restricting social media use during the electoral blackout, which began on July 4 onward, which requires archiving personal posts from official duties and discourages new posts about government actions. Officials view the restrictions as overly cautious, hindering institutional communication on social platforms.

item.title: Após pico de rejeiçăo em embate com Flávio, Michelle reabilita imagem
item.description: Following a peak in rejection during her confrontation with Flávio Bolsonaro, Michelle Bolsonaro began a slow image recovery in July, according to internal tracking used by campaigns and financial market agents. The data show her popularity is rising again after a period of peak wear.

item.title: Segurança pública, eleições e populismo penal – parte 1
item.description: Public security has become the top concern for Brazilians in the 2026 elections, surpassing corruption and the economy. Congress recently approved the Public Security PEC (PEC 18/2025), the Dosimetry Bill (PL 2162/2023), and advanced the PEC to reduce the age of criminal responsibility (PEC 8/2026), reflecting a rise in punitive populism. These initiatives create tensions with recent laws like the Anti-Faction Law and underscore a long-standing pattern of punitive proposals in Brazil since 1988.

item.title: Como resolver o problema da pobreza no Brasil?
item.description: The July 2026 Datafolha poll reveals a significant ideological shift in Brazil, with 44% identifying as right-wing and 39% as left-wing — a 10-point gain for the right and a 10-point loss for the left over four years. This shift is most pronounced among men, evangelicals, and older voters, while attitudes toward poverty have changed dramatically: 40% now associate poverty with laziness (up from 22% in 2022), compared to 58% who see it as stemming from lack of opportunity (down from 76%).

item.title: Após crise com Michelle, Flávio escala esposa para atrair mulheres
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's pre-campaign is increasing the visibility of his wife, Fernanda Bolsonaro, to appeal to female voters and counter the fallout from his estrangement with Michelle Bolsonaro. Fernanda is appearing in social media videos and will contribute to the government platform, focusing on women's health and public healthcare. The team is also considering nominating a woman as vice-presidential candidate to strengthen outreach to female voters.

item.title: Reeleição de Tarcísio no 1º turno pode afetar disputa de Lula e Flávio
item.description: The potential first-round re-election of Tarcísio de Freitas in São Paulo is being closely monitored by both Flávio Bolsonaro's and Lula's campaigns. Flávio's allies see this as advantageous, as Tarcísio could actively support him in a potential runoff without splitting the PT's base in São Paulo. Lula's supporters downplay the impact, referencing the 2006 election and questioning Tarcísio's willingness to campaign for a Bolsonaro candidate.

item.title: Endividamento e ascensão e queda das tiranias: confira livros sobre política e economia que se destacaram no 1º semestre
item.description: In the first half of 2024, books such as 'Parcelado: consumption dynamics in the periphery' by Kauê Lopes dos Santos analyzed the impact of household debt on Lula’s government approval and the electoral race, showing that credit access improved quality of life for low-income populations but led to chronic indebtedness. Simultaneously, works like 'The Internal Threat' by Vladimir Safatle and 'How Tyrants Fall' by Marcelo Dirsus addressed the rise of authoritarianism, arguing that fascism is a potentiality of liberal societies in crisis and offering pathways to dismantle dictatorships.

item.title: Escolha de Sofia
item.description: Despite internal conflicts within the Brazilian right, including family divisions and power struggles in the PL party, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro maintains strong leadership among right-wing voters, positioning himself as a competitive candidate against President Lula in a potential runoff. Unity around his name persists despite tensions between radicalization and moderation, preserving his electoral viability.

item.title: PEC da maioridade penal só deve avançar na Câmara após as eleições
item.description: Chamber of Deputies President Hugo Motta announced the president (Aluísio Mendes) and rapporteur (Mendonça Filho) of the special committee analyzing the constitutional amendment to lower the age of criminal responsibility from 18 to 16. Despite the committee's installation, progress on the proposal remains uncertain, with no voting schedule or guarantee it will reach the plenary before the October elections, as Motta uses committees to address party demands while delaying divisive issues in an election year.

item.title: A segunda conversa de Valdemar com Michelle Bolsonaro após a crise com Flávio
item.description: Valdemar Costa Neto, president of the PL, held a second conversation with Michelle Bolsonaro following the crisis involving Flávio Bolsonaro and Michelle’s exit from PL Mulher. The meeting took place days after the meeting that formalized her departure from the party. The article is subscriber-only and requires registration for full access.

item.title: Falta de policiamento é principal problema da segurança para moradores de SP, aponta Datafolha
item.description: The Datafolha poll shows that 20% of São Paulo residents consider the lack of police presence on the streets as the main public security problem, followed by assaults at 11%. Although this perception has decreased since 2022 (from 24% to 20%), insufficient police staffing remains the top concern, particularly among women (22%) and voters aged 35 to 44 (24%).

item.title: Um ano após carta de Trump a Lula e anúncio de tarifas: relembre os principais capítulos da disputa comercial entre EUA e Brasil
item.description: One year ago, Donald Trump sent a letter to Lula announcing a 50% tariff on Brazilian products, citing Bolsonaro's trial, criticisms of Brazil's Supreme Court, and alleged U.S. trade disadvantage. Despite the claim, Brazil has run a trade deficit with the U.S. since 2009. The move triggered a trade investigation and escalating tensions, with some tariffs revised and others maintained through 2025-2026.

item.title: Caiado critica Bolsonaro e diz que Flávio não deve ser candidato
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado criticized Jair Bolsonaro for his economic management and pandemic response, stating the resulting destabilization was more serious than the electoral defeat. He also declared that Flávio Bolsonaro should not be a presidential candidate due to corruption suspicions in the R$134 million case linked to Banco Master and the 'Dark Horse' film, arguing that insisting on Flávio could help Lula's re-election.

item.title: PF apreende espingarda registrada em nome de Bolsonaro no RS
item.description: Federal Police seized a shotgun registered to Jair Bolsonaro at a man's home in Cachoeirinha, Rio Grande do Sul after he voluntarily came forward to surrender the weapon. The firearm was the last uncollected armament linked to the former president, in compliance with a Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes order investigating potential non-compliance with judicial directives on weapons. The operation coincided with PF searches at Bolsonaro's residence, though no items were found there.

item.title: Flávio foi ‘omisso’ com Michelle, diz ex-ministro de Bolsonaro
item.description: Former minister Ricardo Salles said Flávio Bolsonaro was 'omissive' for failing to restrain attacks by influencers linked to Carlos and Eduardo Bolsonaro against Michelle Bolsonaro, prompting her to release an indignant video. Salles understands Michelle’s reaction, though he questions the timing, and notes that recent episodes involving Flávio are damaging his political image, even if the electoral impact remains unclear.

item.title: Ibaneis anuncia desistência de candidatura ao Senado pelo Distrito Federal
item.description: Governor of the Federal District, Ibaneis Rocha, announced his withdrawal from the Senate race in DF during a press conference on Thursday, March 16, 2023. The statement was made alongside Vice Governor Celina Leão, following his compliance with a Supreme Court (STF) order by Minister Alexandre de Moraes that removed him from office for 90 days due to investigations linked to the January 8 events. Ibaneis did not specify the reasons for his withdrawal but reaffirmed his commitment to local governance.

item.title: Marinho diz que Flávio deve ter o dobro de palanques que o pai
item.description: Senate Opposition Leader Rogério Marinho (PL-RN) stated that Flávio Bolsonaro will likely have double the number of state-level electoral slates compared to the 10 that supported Jair Bolsonaro in 2022, following a meeting between PL and Republicanos to discuss a potential 2026 alliance. Negotiations aim to broaden the coalition and finalize state-level agreements before party conventions, focusing on shared agendas such as amnesty for January 8 defendants, social conservatism, and criticism of the Supreme Federal Court. The rapprochement between the parties reflects an intensification of right-wing priorities in Congress.

item.title: Bolsonaro desestabilizou economia e foi insensível na pandemia, diz Caiado em podcast
item.description: Former Goiás governor Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) criticized Jair Bolsonaro for destabilizing the economy and being insensitive during the pandemic, calling it the main reason for his defeat. He also stated that Flávio Bolsonaro lacks the 'ethical stature' to run for president, citing his appearance at a U.S. government hearing on tariffs and potential corruption links, while avoiding a direct corruption accusation. Caiado suggested that keeping Flávio as the right-wing candidate could ultimately help Lula win in a runoff.

item.title: Haddad diz que SP corre risco de 'começar a ter milícias no interior, como no Rio de Janeiro'
item.description: Fernando Haddad warned that the reduced state presence in public security in São Paulo is leading to the emergence of militias in the interior, similar to Rio de Janeiro, due to private companies selling security services because the state is failing to act. He linked this trend to the state’s fiscal crisis, worsened by low revenue after the Sabesp sale and the effects of the U.S. 'tariff war,' and criticized Tarcísio de Freitas’ administration for inadequate security investment. The remarks were made in an interview with 'Canal do Barão' and coincided with a Ficco operation that dismantled a gang stealing interstate beef shipments.

item.title: A angústia entre aliados bolsonaristas com a campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's pre-campaign is facing growing discontent among Bolsonarist allies due to the lack of a consistent political agenda, electoral strategy, and base mobilization. His trip to the United States to attend a hearing on the 'tariff war' was criticized as a mere social media performance without substantive proposals. Columnist Robson Bonin and figures like Fábio Wajngarten and Ronaldo Caiado argue the campaign lacks structure, ideas, and the capacity to confront opponents.

item.title: Pesquisa indica que Michelle Bolsonaro é apontada como a mulher mais poderosa do país por 15,4% dos entrevistados
item.description: A public opinion poll indicated Michelle Bolsonaro as the most powerful woman in the country, with 15.4% of respondents' mentions. The current first lady, Janja, came in second with 9% of mentions. The survey mapped Brazilians' perception of the most influential female figures in the country.

item.title: Investigação sobre ‘Careca do INSS’ e Lulinha “não deve avançar” até eleições, diz Viana
item.description: Senator Carlos Viana (PSD-MG) stated that the Federal Police informed Supreme Court Justice André Mendonça, the rapporteur of the case, that the investigation involving lobbyist 'Careca do INSS' and businessman Lulinha will not progress before the 2026 elections. The remark implies the case is being delayed to avoid electoral impact.

item.title: Márcio Canella tem prisão mantida e será transferido para Bangu 8
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court upheld the arrest of former Belford Roxo mayor and Senate pre-candidate Márcio Canella after he was caught with a rifle during the 6th phase of Operation Unha e Carne. He will be transferred to Bangu 8 prison in the Gericinó complex, Rio de Janeiro. The probe investigates a money laundering scheme exceeding R$7.6 billion tied to fuel stations and public officials.

item.title: Camilo diz que Alcolumbre e Lula devem se encontrar ainda em julho
item.description: Camilo Santana, PT leader in the Senate, said Lula and Alcolumbre should meet in July to ease tensions and advance key government priorities, including the PEC to end the 6x1 work schedule, the Public Security PEC, and the critical minerals bill. He urged the PT to soften its criticism of Alcolumbre and prioritize dialogue, noting that while passing the 6x1 PEC before recess is unlikely, it could be approved after legislative activities resume in August.

item.title: Novo líder do PT no Senado promete diálogo para melhorar relação entre Lula e Alcolumbre
item.description: Senator Camilo Santana (PT-CE) assumed leadership of the PT in the Senate, promising to improve dialogue between President Lula and Senate President Davi Alcolumbre, whose relationship has been strained since the rejection of Jorge Messias’ STF nomination. He prioritized ending the 6x1 work scale and stressed the need to avoid confrontation and respect institutional prerogatives.

item.title: PF apreende espingarda de Bolsonaro no Rio Grande do Sul
item.description: Federal Police seized the last firearm registered under former President Jair Bolsonaro’s name — a Maestro Arms Company shotgun — in Cachoeirinha, Rio Grande do Sul, while he remains under house arrest. The weapon was held by an importing company, according to his defense. The seizure followed the revocation by Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes of Bolsonaro’s sport shooter and collector registration for 10 firearms.

item.title: Governo responsabiliza setor privado por veto da UE a carnes do Brasil
item.description: The Brazilian government blamed the private sector for the EU's veto on Brazilian meat exports, stating that compliance with European sanitary requirements depends on private control systems implemented by producers. The ban, effective from September 3, was triggered by the use of antimicrobials prohibited in the EU. Nevertheless, the government continues negotiations to reverse the decision.

item.title: Hugo Motta aponta Mendonça Filho para relatoria de PEC que reduz maioridade penal
item.description: Chamber of Deputies President Hugo Motta appointed federal deputy Mendonça Filho (PL-PE) as rapporteur for the Constitutional Amendment Proposal reducing the age of criminal responsibility from 18 to 16 years. The special committee reviewing the proposal will be chaired by Aluisio Mendes (Republicanos-MA) and is set to be installed in the second week of August. The PEC, which had its admissibility approved by the CCJ in June, must still be voted on in the Chamber plenary and the Senate before promulgation, without requiring presidential approval.

item.title: Lula deve receber Alcolumbre para conversa no Alvorada após dois meses e meio sem falar com ele
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has agreed to hold a private meeting with Senate President Davi Alcolumbre after two and a half months of strained relations, with the encounter expected to take place this week at the Palácio da Alvorada. The meeting aims to ease tensions between the Executive and Legislative branches, particularly over the PEC to end the 6x1 work schedule — a key re-election pledge of Lula that Alcolumbre has yet to bring to a vote in the Senate. Government leaders, including Camilo Santana and José Guimarães, are pushing for dialogue to avoid confrontation, despite some PT members labeling Alcolumbre an 'enemy of workers' if he continues to block the proposal.

item.title: Ao tratar de tarifaço dos EUA, Caiado critica Lula por 'provocar' Trump e 'ajoelhamento' de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado criticized President Lula for provoking Donald Trump to gain electoral advantage and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro for sending a document to the U.S. government requesting a delay in tariffs on Brazilian products until the October elections, which Caiado described as 'kneeling' to U.S. interests. He argued Brazil must adopt a sovereign and technically grounded stance in negotiations, advocating for the strengthening of the Itamaraty and rejecting both provocation and submission in foreign policy.

item.title: Procuradoria vê propaganda eleitoral antecipada em fala de Lula sobre pré-candidatas ao Senado
item.description: The Electoral Prosecutor's Office in São Paulo recommended the conviction of President Lula and former ministers Simone Tebet and Marina Silva for alleged premature electoral campaigning during a May government event, where he explicitly asked for votes for the two Senate pre-candidates.

item.title: O aceno de Camilo Santana a Alcolumbre após assumir a liderança do governo no Senado
item.description: Senator Camilo Santana (PT-CE) assumed the government leadership in the Senate and extended an overture to Senate President Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP), calling for dialogue and humility to repair relations after the rejection of Jorge Messias to the STF. He emphasized the need to advance key agendas like ending the 6×1 work scale and the Security PEC, amid rising tensions, including threats from the PT leader in the Chamber to label Alcolumbre an 'enemy of workers'.

item.title: Campanha eleitoral caminha para bater o recorde de mediocridade política
item.description: The 2026 Brazilian electoral campaign is heading toward a record of political mediocrity, reflecting a broader institutional crisis that extends beyond the Executive and Legislative branches to include eroding trust in the Judiciary. Despite structural advantages such as natural resources, a large domestic market, and skilled human capital, public debate remains trapped in sterile polarization, ignoring structural challenges like demography, productivity, organized crime, and external vulnerability. The prevailing perception is that both the exhausted government and a familistic, morally questionable opposition lack ideas and integrity, making solutions to major problems increasingly elusive.

item.title: PDT espera Lula em convenção nacional do partido após atritos com PT
item.description: The PDT confirmed President Lula's (PT) attendance at its national convention on July 20 in Brasília, following recent tensions over state-level alliances. The party seeks to strengthen its position on Fernando Haddad's ticket for São Paulo governor, demanding the first Senate substitute slot. Despite strains — including Lupi's dismissal from the Ministry of Social Security over the INSS scandal — the PDT aims to maintain the progressive front, as seen in Rio Grande do Sul, where it stepped back to support Juliana Brizola's candidacy.

item.title: Senado aprova projeto que amplia crédito a exportadores
item.description: The Senate approved PLV 7/2026, expanding credit for Brazilian exporters through the Brazil Soberano program, offering up to R$15 billion in financing managed by BNDES with risk coverage from FGE. Derived from MP 1.345/2026, the measure was broadened to include agribusiness exporters and associative entities to strengthen resilience against trade shocks such as U.S. tariffs and the Iran war.

item.title: Procuradoria eleitoral vê propaganda antecipada em fala de Lula sobre Tebet e Marina
item.description: The São Paulo Electoral Prosecutor's Office determined that President Lula's statement on May 19, during the launch of the Move Aplicativos program, constituted illegal early electioneering by explicitly requesting votes for Simone Tebet and Marina Silva, who are Senate pre-candidates. Electoral law prohibits explicit vote requests before August 16 of the election year. The final decision rests with the TRE-SP plenary, pending the opinion of reporting judge Danyelle Galvão.

item.title: 'Não podemos sair brigando dentro de casa', diz presidente do PL sobre atritos entre Michelle e Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The national president of the PL, Valdemar Costa Neto, stated that Michelle and Flávio Bolsonaro are not speaking after social media accusations and stressed the need to resolve internal conflicts within 20 days to set a direction ahead of the party's national convention on July 25. He praised Michelle as a special leader and noted that the vice-presidential candidate on Flávio Bolsonaro's ticket remains undefined, emphasizing the need for someone with electoral support and rejecting Daniella Marques due to her lack of votes, despite calling her an excellent person.

item.title: Ibaneis Rocha desiste de concorrer ao Senado pelo Distrito Federal
item.description: Ibaneis Rocha withdrew from the Senate race in the Federal District following the Banco Master scandal, citing family and legal work as reasons. His decision comes amid investigations into the attempted purchase of Banco Master by BRB during his governorship, which caused billions in losses. The withdrawal weakens the right-wing bloc in the DF, especially as Michelle Bolsonaro may also drop out due to internal PL conflicts.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro propõe criação de zona de livre comércio com os EUA e critica relação de Lula com a China
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) proposed the creation of a free trade zone between Brazil and the United States, suggesting Brazil’s inclusion in an agreement similar to USMCA, which he referred to as 'Afta' (Free Trade Agreement of the Americas). During a live stream, he criticized the Lula government for 'licking China’s boots' and prioritizing ideology over national interests, claiming he went to the U.S. to protect Brazil from tariffs and from Lula himself. He also defended the Pix payment system as a Bolsonaro-era initiative and cited corruption scandals involving the current administration.

item.title: Flávio propõe acordo de livre-comércio entre Brasil e EUA
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro proposed Brazil's inclusion in a free-trade agreement modeled after NAFTA, suggesting the creation of an 'Americas Free Trade Agreement' (AFTA) with the U.S., Mexico, and Canada, citing the recent U.S.-Argentina deal as a reference. He criticized the Lula government for failing to send representatives to USTR hearings in Washington, arguing Brazil must be present to defend its interests and attract American investment.

item.title: STF confirma constitucionalidade de repasses mínimos de 30% para cotas raciais nas eleições
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court (STF) upheld the constitutionality of Constitutional Amendment No. 133/2024, which establishes a minimum 30% allocation of the Special Campaign Financing Fund (FEFC) and the Party Fund for Black and mixed-race candidates in elections. The ruling rejected petitions from entities arguing for a higher percentage, such as 55.5% proportional to the Afro-descendant population, stating that defining the index is a legislative prerogative, while the STF only assesses constitutionality. The 30% floor is mandatory, but parties may increase it voluntarily.
